### Loops record why they stop: a stop that leaves a brief's status working gets a turn to set it, and run-streams.sh no longer counts it as done

change `kppsnzynkzyp` · [log `bf3ed266eb83`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e9be5afb-09c9-4473-a9e9-38f2fb61ca80/bf3ed266eb837309000a993b4a220cf0d056fc361da3b2f51cf7a73527ad07c2.jsonl.gz)

On 2026-11-08 three application-core streams (objects, environment, reuse) ended with their briefs still at 'Status: working'. Each session decided 'LOOP: stop' in feature-loop.sh's decision turn and wrote the status it meant there ('waiting on jobs ...', 'blocked: ...'), but that turn may not edit or commit, and the cycle before it was never asked to keep the status line current. feature-loop.sh then exited 0, and run-streams.sh counted a clean stop with no status as done, so objects and reuse were never rerun when their jobs came back, and the merge loop refused the reconcile.

feature-loop.sh: the cycle instruction now asks the session to keep a brief's '- Status:' line current in each commit; the decision turn is told a status is never its last line; and when the session decides to stop while the status still says working, one more turn before the compact sets the status the brief's Loop until gives and commits it. If that leaves the status working or uncommitted, the loop ends with exit 1, as needing attention. run-streams.sh: a clean stop whose status is neither done, blocked nor waiting on jobs is now run once more, like a failure, and counts as blocked the second time.

Verified with bash -n on both scripts and a stubbed test of brief_status, has_status and close_status: a stop with status working that the session fixes and commits (ok), one it leaves alone (failed), one edited but not committed (failed), an already blocked status and a brief with no status line (no turn). The stream workspaces run their own copy of feature-loop.sh, so the same file is committed in each before the rerun.

### feature-loop.sh finds a brief in its own workspace first, so a stream reads and is pointed at its own copy

change `unwrvwqwzxqq` · [log `4b7b18b3c08d`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e9be5afb-09c9-4473-a9e9-38f2fb61ca80/4b7b18b3c08d2fdb5e14e88536370bcba974c50ff5bb4a4f4457f2d8f45300e7.jsonl.gz)

run-streams.sh starts each stream's copy of feature-loop.sh with the default workspace as its current directory, and feature-loop.sh looked a relative brief up from there first. Every stream therefore ran with the default workspace's copy of its brief: the cycle instruction pointed the session at it, the brief-changed check hashed it, and since kppsnzyn close_status read its status from it. No stream edits that copy, so its Progress is the launch-time one. In this morning's rerun the objects and environment sessions set their status in their own copies; close_status read 'working' in the default copy, asked for an extra turn, and ended the loops as needing attention, with exit 1. run-streams.sh reads each stream's own copy, so both still came out blocked. The objects session diagnosed this in its run summary.

A relative brief is now looked up under the script's own repo first and then from the caller's directory, and named relative to the repo as before. Verified by running the resolution with the objects workspace as the root and the default workspace as the current directory (it gives the workspace's own llm-dlc/loops/application-core-objects.md), with the default workspace as the root, and with an absolute path. The file was replaced by rename, since run-streams.sh is running. The reuse stream, still running, keeps the old behaviour until it stops, and the stream workspaces' copies get this change at the merge.

### application-core objects O3: the frozen throttle claims bound allocations at 1, the user's decision, so the contract's O3 passes

The frozen throttle claims (throttle-constructed-claim, throttle-setup-claim) said allocations 0 in both versions, but Throttle#allows makes the IllegalArgumentException it throws for negative units. The domain gate counts every allocation on any path, so the contract's O3 came out unresolved instead of expected.json's verdicts. Phase 0 already counted such a throw in checked-claim (bound 1), so the user decided the 0 was a slip: both claims are now bounded at 1 in each version, and expected.json is unchanged. The user also decided that the bound covers the target call only: setup calls are bounded by the plan's setup_calls and their outcomes are compared, so their allocations aren't counted, and the gate stays as it is.

The stream's test helper throttle_claim, which raised the bound to 1 to work around the fixture, now asserts it instead. Verified inline: tests/application_core.rs 14 of 14 (13 before, O3 failing), tests/application_core_objects.rs 21 passed and 1 ignored (the cache test that waits on the reuse stream, as before). The brief's Progress records the decision, and the status is blocked only on O2's String adapter, which waits for the merge. Made by the user's session from the default workspace while this stream's loop was stopped.

The last of interface request 6 (the objects stream's: give compare a plan per subject). Before, compare built every kernel claim with no domain, so on the throttle family's after-setup defect (one unit short only once a setup call has taken some) it verified Throttle#allows over the constructor domain, and had no way to state the setup plan's domain. Now compare --domains FILE takes a JSON object from each kernel subject (the new method, pkg.Class#method) to its ObjectDomain, as a frozen claim states one; the subject's claim carries it as it is, so spec::heap::check_with enforces or refuses each part. With it, the serde hole cycle 13 closed in spec/plans.rs is closed in spec/mod.rs: ObjectDomain, VersionBounds, ObjectBounds and Construction had no deny_unknown_fields, so a domain with a misspelt option (nulable) was read as the domain without it. ## Conversation

Each prompt with the final reply to it, shortened where long. The [log](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e9be5afb-09c9-4473-a9e9-38f2fb61ca80/8eb05e296a25581c1dcd6b09b80617979ab79bf0cd844140925aae6c4ae11ac6.jsonl.gz) has every step in between: reasoning, tool calls and their results.

### 1. 2026-11-08 11:26 UTC

> The latest feature streams ("application-core") appear to have exited early. Can you investigate?

**Reply:**

Three of the four streams stopped early because of a design gap in `feature-loop.sh`: a session decides to stop at a point where it isn't allowed to write that decision into its brief. Nothing crashed. Nothing is running now (no loop processes, no `feature-loop-*` scopes).

## How it happens

1. Each cycle does one piece of work and commits it. The cycle instruction asks the session to update Progress with "what this piece did and what comes next". It never asks it to set the `- Status:` line.
2. After the commit, `decide()` (`llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh:423`) asks a separate question: "continue or stop?" That turn is explicitly forbidden to edit or commit.
3. The streams' "Loop until" rules say "*stop with* `waiting on jobs ID …` / `blocked: …`". The sessions only realise this applies in the decision turn. They answer `LOOP: stop` and put the status they meant in the reply text, where nothing reads it.
4. `feature-loop.sh` exits 0 and logs "the session decided the work was done". Then `run-streams.sh:352` sees exit 0 with `Status: working` and counts the stream as **done**: "its status doesn't say why: counted as done".

## What each stream said in its last decision turn

| Stream | Stopped | What it meant | What the brief says |
|---|---|---|---|
| objects | 07:44, after 10 cycles | `waiting on jobs 20261108-072230… 20261108-074116…` | `working` |
| environment | 06:13, after 3 cycles | `blocked: E3 and the Q integration wait on objects/values` | `working` |

### 2. 2026-11-08 11:29 UTC

> Implement the fix, then restart the loop in tmux

**Reply:**

I fixed both scripts and restarted the run. It's going in a new tmux session called `application-core`; attach with `tmux attach -t application-core`. Objects, environment and reuse started their first cycle at 11:33. Values stays finished because its status is `blocked`, and the merge loop will run once the three are finished. `run-streams.sh` also started the verification loop.

## The fix (`kppsnzyn`)
- **`feature-loop.sh`:**
  - Every cycle is now asked to keep the brief's `- Status:` line current in its own commit.
  - If the session says `LOOP: stop` while the status still reads `working`, it gets one more turn before compacting, in which it sets the real status and commits it. If it doesn't manage that, the loop exits 1 instead of reporting the work as done.
  - The decision turn is now told that a line like `waiting on jobs …` doesn't count as its answer. That's how the reuse stream's earlier 04:34 run got stuck.
- **`run-streams.sh`:** a clean stop with a status other than done, blocked or waiting on jobs is now rerun once. Before, it counted as done. A second such stop counts as blocked.
